lines.text: In 1925, one con artist sold the entire Eiffel Tower.
Then came back weeks later and sold it again.
See, Paris newspapers joked the tower cost too much to paint,
so Victor Lustig printed fake government letters,
inviting six scrap dealers to a secret hotel meeting.
Inside a luxury suite, he whispered the big lie:
the city was secretly tearing down seven thousand tons of iron,
and picking one buyer for the famous landmark.
One dealer wanted the metal contract so badly
he handed over a suitcase full of cash, plus a bribe.
Lustig jumped on the next train out of France,
waiting for police headlines that never came.
Because the victim was way too embarrassed to tell anyone.
So Lustig bought a fresh ticket right back to Paris,
slapped another price tag on the tower, and cashed in twice.
